targetReport.description: Angola's organic law establishing autarquias locais (decentralized local authorities) — genuinely distinct from ao-lei-administracao-local-15-16's deconcentrated state-administration framework. Verified via OCR of the scanned Diário da República I Série N.º 134 (8 August 2017), hosted by FAOLEX. Art. 22 (Princípio da Autonomia Financeira e Patrimonial): "1. Os órgãos autónomos do Poder Local gozam de plena liberdade de decisão e gestão dos recursos financeiros e do seu património nos termos da Constituição e da lei. 2. Os recursos financeiros das Autarquias Locais devem ser proporcionais às atribuições previstas pela Constituição ou por lei... 3. A lei estabelece que uma parte dos recursos financeiros das Autarquias Locais deve ser proveniente de rendimentos e de impostos locais." Art. 30(2) mandates direct election: "A Assembleia da Autarquia é composta por representantes locais, eleitos por sufrágio universal, livre, directo, secreto e periódico." CRITICALLY, Art. 41 (Princípio do Gradualismo e da Transitoriedade) makes actual rollout contingent on further state action, not automatic: "A institucionalização efectiva das Autarquias Locais obedece ao Princípio do Gradualismo" — "consiste na faculdade dos órgãos competentes do Estado determinarem por lei a oportunidade da sua criação." This gradualism clause is the textual root of why, per ao-lei-13-20-regime-financeiro-autarquias's own dropped note below, no operational autarquia has yet been activated.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

targetReport.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
targetReport.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.
targetReport.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not from a stated rate — see _open_questions. Adopted 25 May 2009; EUR-Lex lists exactly two consolidated versions, 19/08/2010 and 01/09/2014, with 01/09/2014 flagged as the current version. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

targetReport.title: Local Government Act, 2002 (No. 5 of 2002)
targetReport.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23, confirmed s.130's referenced finance law is the Local Government Finance and Audit Act 2004, added verbatim s.130 text): The Gambia's Local Government Act. Directly verified via pdftotext extraction, Part VII (Financial Provisions), Section 128: "(1) The revenue and funds of a Council include all sums of money or funds accruing to a Council. (2) The revenue and funds of a Council shall be applied to the administration, development and welfare of the inhabitants within its Area of jurisdiction. (3) The Central Government shall provide twenty-five per cent of the Council's development budget." Section 131 separately grants Councils independent rating/taxation power (General Rates Act, 1992); Section 130 defers detailed financial regulation to a not-yet-located "Local Government (Finance and Audit)" law, stating in full: "The financial affairs of a Council shall be regulated in accordance with a Local Government (Finance and Audit) law to be enacted by the National Assembly." This referenced law was confirmed this round (AF/G.23) to be the "Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004" — cited by name and year in two independent primary Gambian government sources (the National Audit Office's audit report on Kanifing Municipal Council, see gm-nao-audit-kmc-2017-2019, and Kanifing Municipal Council's own budget page, see gm-kmc-budget-2021) — though its full text could not be located online at any government, NGO, or legal-database source despite exhaustive search (NAO's own "Laws & Standards" listing page omits it). No broader equalisation/formula-based revenue-sharing mechanism across the 5 divisions was found beyond this single 25% development-budget clause.
targetReport.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.
